source_text: Haec postulans ac deprecans David, ad virgam, quae ex ipso pulcherrimi illius fructus florem germinatura erat, vaticinans dicebat: Audi filia, et vide, et inclina aurem tuam; et obliviscere populum tuum, et domum patris tui: et concupiscet rex decorem tuum: quoniam ipse est Dominus Deus tuus, et adorabis eum. Audi filia, quae antea in te praedicta sunt: ut et cognitionis oculis res ipsas contempleris. Audi me, tibi praesignificantem; et Archangelum perfecta tibi mysteria diserte adnuntiantem.
thought_title: David addresses the daughter about the king
orientation: David the prophet is speaking in prophecy to the branch that is to bring forth the fruit, continuing the appeal to honor the Virgin.
pass_a_gloss: Requesting and earnestly entreating these things, David was saying, prophesying to the branch which from him was about to sprout the flower of that most beautiful fruit: Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear; and forget your people and the house of your father: and the king will desire your beauty: for he himself is the Lord your God, and you will worship him. Hear, daughter, the things which were foretold before concerning you: so that with the eyes of knowledge you may also contemplate the realities themselves. Hear me foretokening to you; and the Archangel clearly announcing to you the complete mysteries.

choices.why: keeps the plant image that carries germinatura and florem in the same clause
literal sense of decor here as the visible beauty the king desires
preserves future indicative force and direct object, following quoniam ipse est Dominus Deus tuus

bible_refs.note: quoted source words: Audi filia, et vide, et inclina aurem tuam; et obliviscere populum tuum, et domum patris tui: et concupiscet rex decorem tuum: quoniam ipse est Dominus Deus tuus, et adorabis eum; LXX Psalm 44:11-12

pass_b_english: As he requested this and earnestly entreated for it, David spoke in prophecy to the branch that would spring from him bearing the flower of that most beautiful fruit, saying: "Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father's house, and the king will desire your beauty, for he himself is the Lord your God, and you will worship him" (Psalm 45:10-11).

David continues: "Listen, daughter, to what was foretold about you before, so that you may see the realities themselves with the eyes of knowledge. Listen to me, who foreshadows this for you, and to the Archangel, who clearly announces to you the perfect mysteries."

problems.quote: Listen, daughter, to what was foretold about you before, so that you may see the realities themselves with the eyes of knowledge. Listen to me, who foreshadows this for you, and to the Archangel, who clearly announces to you the perfect mysteries.
problems.source_quote: Audi filia, quae antea in te praedicta sunt: ut et cognitionis oculis res ipsas contempleris. Audi me, tibi praesignificantem; et Archangelum perfecta tibi mysteria diserte adnuntiantem.
problems.why: Closing the quotation marks after the Psalm makes this unquoted paragraph sound like the homilist speaking, hiding that David is still the speaker ('me, who foreshadows').
problems.fix: David continues: "Listen, daughter, to what was foretold about you before, to see the realities with eyes of knowledge. Listen to me, who foreshadow this for you, and to the Archangel clearly announcing the perfect mysteries."
problems.ruling: Latin vaticinans dicebat continues; Audi me, tibi praesignificantem is still David speaking, not the homilist.
